acceptance: A read overtaken by a save receipt or a newer accepted read is revalidated with a fresh read instead of restoring old content, and a failed obsolete read neither clears the current text nor schedules an extra read; a delayed read after a save does not conflict with the next edit; a genuine return to earlier disk bytes is adopted as an external update; reads of other documents and storages stay independent; reads of a closed or replaced document are neither retried nor published.
A nested Explorer node and its folder are found by their paths; a missing path is not.

A change reaches only the documents it names in its own storage (equal paths in another storage are untouched); a change without paths refreshes that storage's open documents; an outside-root, unknown or overflowing watcher change degrades to a revalidation of the root.

reason: TS allocates parse workers per owner through a scheduler: one allocation per owner at a time, cancelled queued work never allocated, asynchronous allocations accounted until their exit is confirmed, failed exits retried on retirement, oversized input refused before allocating and queue waits bounded. Native document work runs on one bounded thread pool with per-request generations (documents::tests::dp41_dp42_bounded_executor_thread_ceiling_and_exact_deadline_scheduling) and oversized sources are refused before reading, so there are no worker allocations to account for or exit.

acceptance: A view never goes away with typing that is not yet stored: a dirty editor stays live (never hibernated) and closing or switching documents snapshots the newest text and drains it before the view is released; an external update adopted while a view is away (also after edits were undone) is what the next view shows, and an older in-flight write is retired before newer input is written over the adopted text.

reason: TS sessions also run in a manual save mode that the desktop never uses (every desktop host passes saveMode="auto"; manual is the shared library default and performance harnesses'), and they publish whether a window holds unsaved edits through an exported subscription nothing in the product reads. The native desktop autosaves every document and has neither.
React StrictMode mounts, unmounts and remounts effects in development, so TS must not retire a document session during that cleanup/setup probe. GPUI views have no such probe.

TS coordinates a window close across the Electron main process and its renderer: it ignores a flush acknowledgement forged by another renderer and must not touch a destroyed BrowserWindow that closes before it is ready. The product never configures its close-choice question (resolveCloseChoice defaults to save), so the ask / don't-save / cancel / ask-again / asking-failed paths are unreachable. The native close drains documents in process and asks only when a document could not be saved.

TS's renderer persists a document through an IPC adapter that must forward the session's base version to the authorized conditional write and carry the structured conflict, not-found, permission-denied and io outcomes back across the process boundary. Native sessions call the workspace provider in process with typed results (editor::document_session tests cover conditional writes and each outcome).
